resources.string: Find it on the PS5 under Settings > Network > Connection Status > View Connection Status. Tap here to enter it.
Find it on the PS4 under Settings > Network > View Connection Status. Tap here to enter it.
Nothing answers at this address. Check the IP, that the %1$s is awake on the same Wi-Fi, and that %2$s is running.
Not answering: %1$s. Start it on the console, or check its port.
Not answering: %1$s. Start them on the console, or check their ports.
Find it on the PS5 under Settings > Network > Connection Status > View Connection Status.
Find it on the PS4 under Settings > Network > View Connection Status.
Connection lost. Trying again in %1$d s…
Set the console\'s IP address first. Tap the card at the top.
Check the console\'s IP address and the FTP port.
The page wants to open %1$s. Ads often trigger this when you tap a link, so only continue if you expected it.

The installer needs a direct package link the console can open without logging in. FTP works for any file and keeps your login session. The phone relays the data in the background, with progress above the bottom bar and in a notification. The payload shelf keeps a small payload (up to %1$s) inside the app for the Payload tab.
The console downloads the packages straight from this phone over Wi-Fi, so nothing is copied to it first. The phone and the console must be on the same network.
Waiting for the console to start downloading…
The console has downloaded all of it
If the console never starts downloading, the Wi-Fi may be stopping devices from reaching each other (guest networks often do). Use the main network, and let this app run in the background.
Can\'t find this phone\'s Wi-Fi address. Connect it to the same Wi-Fi as the console.
Sharing stopped because nothing was downloaded for a long time.
Progress shows above the bottom bar and in a notification. It keeps going if you leave the app.
Set the console\'s IP address (tap the card at the top) and a valid FTP port to browse its files.
That name is already used here.
This deletes the folder and everything inside it from the console. It can\'t be undone.
This deletes the file from the console. It can\'t be undone.
The name can\'t contain slash characters.
The name has characters that aren\'t allowed.
Can\'t reach the FTP server. Check the console IP and the FTP port (etaHEN\'s built-in FTP uses 1337, the FTP payload uses 2121).
Can\'t reach the FTP server. Check the console IP and the FTP port (GoldHEN\'s FTP uses 2121).
the folder is nested too deeply
Cancelled. A partial file may remain at %1$s
Cancelled. The partial download was discarded.
Gave up after the connection kept failing. Last error: %1$s
The console kept only %1$s of the %2$s that were sent.
The connection closed before the whole file arrived.
Couldn\'t create the file in Downloads
Couldn\'t open the new file for writing
That file is bigger than %1$s, so it wasn\'t added to the shelf.
That file is %1$s. The shelf takes payloads up to %2$s.
It is deleted from the shelf. The original file on your phone isn\'t touched.
Nothing saved yet. Add the payloads you use often (an FTP server, %1$s, ...) and send each with one tap. You can also save one straight from the Web tab when you download it.
Its saved IP address and ports are removed. Your other consoles are not affected.
The site is busy or down right now (error %1$s). Try again in a moment.
No bookmarks yet. Open a page and tap %1$s.
Tap a bookmark to open it. %1$s makes it your homepage.
Blocked so far: %1$d. Networks in the built-in list: %2$d. Reload the page after changing anything.
Your own domains, one per line
Ad block: on · blocked: %1$d · tap to change
Ad block: off · blocked: %1$d · tap to change
Nothing answers at the console\'s address.

• Check the IP address on the %1$s (Settings > Network > Connection Status). It can change after a restart.\n• Wake the console fully. Rest mode often turns the network off.\n• Use the same Wi-Fi on both. Guest networks and VPNs block it.
The console answered, but nothing listens on that port.

• Start etaHEN on the console. It provides the installer (12800), the loader (9021) and FTP (1337).\n• A separate FTP payload usually uses 2121. Enter the same port here.\n• On the console card, the light that is off shows what is missing.

• Start GoldHEN on the console. It provides the loader (9090) and FTP (2121).\n• To install packages, also run flatz\'s Remote Package Installer on the console (12800).\n• On the console card, the light that is off shows what is missing.
The console\'s FTP server rejected the user name or password.
• %2$s accepts the user name anonymous with any password.\n• If you set a login on the console, enter it under Upload.\n• The password isn\'t saved. Enter it again after restarting the app.
The link to the console broke or stopped moving data. The app retries and continues where it stopped.
• Keep the phone near the router and the console awake.\n• Pause other big downloads on the network.\n• If it keeps failing, wait a moment and tap Try again.
The installer didn\'t take the link
The console is reachable, but its installer refused this link.

• The link must lead straight to the package file and open without a login.\n• The console must be able to reach it. Links from this phone only work on the same Wi-Fi.\n• Check that the installer is running and the console has free space.
The console kept less than was sent. The drive is usually full or read-only.
• Free some space on the console.\n• Choose another folder, for example on a USB drive.\n• Then tap Try again.
That folder or file was refused
The FTP server can\'t open, write or change it here.
• Check that the folder exists. Names are case-sensitive.\n• System folders are read-only. Use /data or a USB drive.\n• A file used by a running game may be locked. Close the game.
The phone can\'t use the file
The file is gone or moved, the app lost access to it, or the phone is out of space.
• Choose the file again.\n• Free some storage on the phone.\n• For a file in a cloud app, save it to the phone first.
The website did not hand over the file. The link may have expired, need a login, or the site is busy.
• Start the download again from the Web tab. That keeps your login.\n• Links from file-hosting sites often expire after a few minutes.\n• If the site reported an error in the 500s, try again later.
No release found on the Releases page yet.
Check for updates when the app opens
The check asks GitHub for the newest release, at most once a day. Nothing about you or your consoles is sent; GitHub sees your IP address, as any website does.
• Turn the console fully on (not rest mode) and start %1$s.\n• Use the same Wi-Fi on the phone and the console. Guest networks and VPNs keep devices apart.\n• Then scan again.
This phone isn\'t on a Wi-Fi network. Connect it to the same Wi-Fi as the console, then scan again.
Tap Use to set the address of %1$s.
Only your Wi-Fi network is scanned, on a few console ports. Nothing is sent over the internet.
Copies the app version, your phone model and the last message, to paste into a bug report. IP addresses and links are left out.
Saves your consoles, homepage, bookmarks, ad list and payloads in one file. FTP passwords are not saved.
Payloads left out because the file would be too large: %1$d
That file is not a Bento backup.
That backup was made by a newer version of Bento. Update the app, then try again.
Your consoles, homepage, bookmarks and ad list are replaced by the ones in the file. Payloads in the file are added to the shelf. You will need to type your FTP passwords again.
Payloads that could not be stored: %1$d
No web link on the clipboard.
Only addresses that start with http:// or https:// are sent. Left out: %1$d
A chain sends several payloads one after the other, with a pause after each. Press and hold the app icon to start one of the first four chains from your home screen.
This launcher can\'t add shortcuts. Press and hold the app icon to find your chains there.
Waiting for the console to be ready…
Stopped at step %1$d (%2$s). Payloads sent: %3$d of %4$d
Set the console\'s IP address and the loader port first.
Not on the shelf any more: %1$s. Add it again or edit the chain.
That chain doesn\'t exist any more.
The app closed before these were done. Continue starts each one again from the beginning.
Files not found any more, choose them again: %1$d
Slows transfers down so the Wi-Fi stays free for other things. A change takes effect right away.
This deletes the selected files and folders from the console, folders with everything inside them. It can\'t be undone.
Items deleted: %1$d, not deleted: %2$d. The first problem: %3$s
Files: %1$d, together %2$s. They are saved in Downloads/%3$s, in the same folders as on the console.
Links inside folders are not downloaded: %1$d.
Files taken: %1$d. The folders hold more than that, or go deeper than the app follows.
There is no file to download in the selection.
Nothing in this folder matches the search.
Too many tabs. The limit is %1$d. Close one first.

A cheat engine for your games: find a value (health, money, ammo), change it or freeze it. Send the debugger payload from the Payload tab first (ps5debug-NG on a PS5, ps4debug-NG on a PS4), then tap Connect.
To try it without a PS5: run fake_console.py in Termux, use 127.0.0.1 as the IP address and 7744 as the port.
No memory regions found for this process.
Set the console\'s IP address (tap the card at the top) to connect.
Nothing answered on port %1$d. Send the debugger (ps5debug-NG or ps4debug-NG) from the Payload tab first, then tap Connect again.
Bento kept the bytes around this address, so Find again can find it after the game restarts.
Bento has no bytes around this address to find it again. Tap Make findable while the game runs.
Cheat files for this game (the one for your version is tinted):
%1$d cheats. The game is loaded at %2$s.
Not changed: the game\'s code there is not what the cheat file expects. The file is probably for another version of the game.
The debugger did not say which game this is (no title ID), so there is no cheat file to look up.
This file is for version %1$s; the game is %2$s. Cheats may not work, and Bento refuses to change code that does not match.
Where the cheat files are read from: a folder with json.txt and a json folder, like the PS5_Cheats repository. The fake console serves its own at http://127.0.0.1:12800/cheats/.
No cheat has the bytes Bento needs to find it again.
Found again: %1$d moved, %2$d already right, %3$d not found.
The console is back; freezing goes on.
Lost the console; trying again (frozen values pause until it is back)…
Enter bytes in hex, for example 64 00 00 00.
Change the bytes and tap Write. Fewer bytes than shown changes only those.
Tap a line to change its bytes.
Paste cheats someone shared from Bento. Cheats this game has already are skipped.
No cheats found in that text.

The console keeps this search because it is big. Change the value in the game and narrow it down with Decreased, Increased, Changed or Unchanged. Once few enough are left, they come over to the phone.
Not supported yet (it uses a code section).
The console has no room to remember that many values. Turn on Skip slow memory, or search for a value you know.
Remembered %1$d values. Now change the value in the game and use Next scan.

For values the game shows as a bar or not at all: the console remembers every value now. Then change it in the game (take damage, spend some) and tap Next scan with Decreased, Increased, Changed or Unchanged, until few are left.
Unknown-value scans need ps5debug-NG 1.3 or newer.
More than %1$d matches: too many to keep. Search for a more unusual value (for example after it changed) and try again.
That is not a valid %1$s value.
Start a game on the console, then tap Refresh: scans search the game in the foreground.
Showing the first %1$d. Narrow it down with another scan to see them all; then their values update live.
No cheats for this game yet. Find a value with Scan, tap it and choose Add to cheats. Turn on Freeze to keep a value from changing.
Enter an address in hex, for example 20001234.
This address is outside the regions the process has mapped; it reads as zeros.
Your phone\'s remote for a jailbroken PS5 or PS4. Install games and apps, send payloads, move files and cheat in games, all over Wi-Fi.
A jailbroken console running etaHEN (PS5) or GoldHEN (PS4), on the same Wi-Fi as this phone. Bento talks to the tools already on the console; it changes nothing on it by itself.
Install packages (.pkg) on the console from a web link, or straight from this phone.
Send payloads (.elf, .bin) to the console. Keep your favourites on a shelf and run several in a row.
Copy files from this phone to the console over FTP.
Browse the console\'s files: open folders, download, rename, delete.
A browser for homebrew sites. Send a link to the console or download it to the phone.
A cheat engine: find values in a game, change or freeze them, and use ready-made cheat files.
Tap the card at the top and enter the console\'s IP address, or let Find my console look for it.
When the lights on the card turn green, the console is ready. Pick a tab and go.
Not sure what something does? Tap the small ? next to it.
You can open this page again from About (the Bento name at the top).

Bento needs the console\'s IP address on your Wi-Fi. On a PS5: Settings → Network → View Connection Status → IPv4 Address. Or tap Find my console to search for it. The three lights on the card show what answers: the installer, the payload loader and FTP.

Paste one or more links to .pkg files (one per line, or any text that has links in it) and tap Send. The console downloads and installs them by itself. Accepted links leave the box and show up under Recent, so you can send them again with one tap.
The port of the package installer on the console: 12800 for etaHEN\'s installer on a PS5, and for the Remote Package Installer app on a PS4. Leave it as it is unless you changed it on the console.
Pick .pkg files on this phone and Bento shares them on your Wi-Fi; the console downloads them from the phone. Keep Bento open (or let it run in the background) until the console has finished.
Where the console listens for payloads: 9021 for etaHEN on a PS5, 9090 for GoldHEN on a PS4.
Payloads you use often, kept inside Bento: add a file once, then send it with one tap. Remove takes it off the shelf only, not from your phone.
A chain sends several payloads in a row, with a pause between them (for example a jailbreak payload, then etaHEN, then a tool). Pin a chain to your home screen to start it from there.
Bento moves files with the console\'s FTP server. etaHEN uses port 1337 (or 2121 for ftpsrv), GoldHEN 2121. The user is usually anonymous with no password. The folder is where uploads go.
Choose one or more files on this phone and tap Upload; they go into the folder in FTP settings, one after the other. A transfer that breaks off can be continued later.
Tap a folder to open it and a file for what you can do with it. Hold a file to pick several. Pin folders you use often. The FTP settings are the same as on the Upload tab.
Browse homebrew sites. Tap a link to a .pkg or a payload and Bento offers to send it to the console or download it. More has bookmarks, find in page, the home page, the ad block and desktop mode.
The page Home opens, and the first page when Bento starts.
Leaves out ads and pop-ups, which on download sites are often fake download buttons.
Shows sites as they look on a computer, for pages whose phone version leaves things out.

The Memory tab works with a debugger payload you send from the Payload tab: ps5debug-NG on a PS5 or ps4debug-NG on a PS4 (older ps4debug works too, with fewer extras). It answers on port 744 and tells the console\'s screen when it is loaded. Use offline games only: changing memory in online games can get your account banned.

How the game stores the number. Most counters (health, money, ammo) are 4 bytes. Speeds, positions and bars are often Float. Try 4 bytes first, then Float, then 2 bytes. Tap a match to see its bytes read as every type.

1. Search for the number the game shows now (Exact value).
2. Change it in the game: take damage, spend money.
3. Enter the new number and tap Next scan.
4. Repeat until a few matches are left, then tap one to change it.

No number on screen (a bar)? Start with Unknown value, then use Decreased, Increased, Changed or Unchanged after each change. Between finds a range, for when you only know about where the number is.
Graphics memory is big and reads slowly, and game values are hardly ever there. Skipping it makes scans much faster. If a value is not found, turn this off and search again.

Every place in the game\'s memory that still fits. The first 200 are listed with their value and their value at the scan before; with 200 or fewer they update live. Tap one to write a value, add it to your cheats, watch it or see it in memory.
Addresses you watch stay at the top of Scan with their live value, while you go on searching. Tap one to write a value, save it as a cheat or stop watching it.

Ready-made cheats from the community cheat files etaHEN uses (the PS5_Cheats repository), found by the game\'s title ID and version. Switch a cheat on or off; Apply cheats run once. Bento checks the game\'s code before it changes anything, and refuses when it does not match (another game version).

Addresses you found and saved, for this game. Tap one to change its value, write it once, watch it or remove it. Groups keep long lists tidy. Share sends them to a friend as text; Import adds a shared list.

Writes the value again five times a second, so the game cannot change it: health that never goes down. Freezing goes on while Bento is in the background (a notification shows it), and picks up again after the console wakes from rest mode.

Addresses move when a game restarts. Bento keeps the bytes around each cheat; Find all again looks for them in memory and moves each cheat to where its bytes are now. It works for most values, not all: if one is not found, search for it again.
Every process on the console. Open one to see its memory regions (rwx: read, write, run; writable ones are tinted) and a region for its bytes. Tap a line of bytes to change them, or Go to an address.
What the console\'s system and payloads print, live. ps5debug-NG sends it on port 3232. Handy when a payload or a cheat misbehaves.
Nothing answered on port %1$d. Send ps5debug-NG first; it sends the console\'s log there.
No lines yet. Tap Start, then do something on the console.

Shows the console\'s own log as it is written: messages from the system, from etaHEN and from payloads. Start connects to port 3232 (ps5debug-NG serves it). Pause holds the screen still while lines keep coming in; Follow keeps the newest line in sight. Type in the filter to see only lines with that text, and Copy to paste the lines into a bug report.
Looking for installed games and apps…
Check a package on this phone
The site only sends whole files, so Bento can\'t look inside without downloading all of it.
A PS5 package keeps its name and icon encrypted, so only its size is shown.

A backup is a copy of this game\'s save folder on your phone. It can go back onto this console for the same user, for example after you deleted the game or to undo a bad save. Saves are locked to the console and account that made them.
%1$d files are on their way to Downloads/%3$s/%2$s.
%1$d files from \"%2$s\" go into the save folder of %3$s. Files with the same name there are replaced.
That folder\'s name doesn\'t start with %1$s. Make sure it is a backup of this game.
Close the game first. Back up the current save before you replace it.
%1$d files are on their way. Start the game when the transfer is done.
Pick a folder on this phone and a folder on the console. Sync sends only what is new or changed.
Where on the console should it go? The folder is made if it isn\'t there.
Bento can no longer read that folder. Remove it and add it again.
%1$d new files, %2$d changed, %3$d already there. %4$s to send.
%1$d folders will be made on the console.
There are very many files; only the first 20000 are compared.
Nothing is deleted, on the phone or on the console.

Everything installed on the console, with its name, icon and version, read from the console\'s own records (/user/appmeta). Tap one to open its folder, see its saves or copy its title ID (handy for cheat files and patches). Icons are kept on the phone, so the list is quicker the next time.

Your saves, per user and game. Back up copies a game\'s save folder to Downloads on this phone. Put a backup back sends a folder you pick on the phone into the game\'s save folder. Saves are locked to the console and account that made them, so a backup only works on the same console for the same user. Close the game before you put a save back.
Opens the folder where the console keeps screenshots and video clips (/user/av_contents). Tick the ones you want and tap Download: they land in Downloads on this phone.

For a folder you add to again and again, like your packages or homebrew. Add a folder from the phone and say where it goes on the console. Sync compares the two and sends only the files the console doesn\'t have, or has with another size. Nothing is ever deleted. Bento remembers the folders for each console.

Shows what a .pkg is before you install it: name, icon, title ID, version, whether it is a game, an update or an add-on, and the firmware it needs. For a web link only a few small pieces are read, not the whole file. PS5 packages keep this encrypted, so for them only the size is shown.
